items.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: this trumpet player came in and we finished the rehearsal and ran to the nearest bar I think, the whole band, en masse. The trumpet player was shaking his head and I said, “John, what’s wrong?”

ctx.x: Describe that for us. Kind of give us a hypothetical.

Well his standards were so high. In fact one trumpet player at the trumpet player’s first rehearsal, I think I’d made two or three rehearsals, this trumpet player came in and we finished the rehearsal and ran to the nearest bar I think, the whole band, en masse. The trumpet player was shaking his head and I said, “John, what’s wrong?” He said, “I can’t figure this guy out.” I said, “who, Goodman?” He said, “yeah.” I said, “well what can’t you figure out?” And he said, “well he wants everything to swing, but he…

eight bars like this silently, and then we came in [snaps fingers] about like that, I mean almost exactly but not quite, and we thought he was going to bite our heads off and he started laughing. He thought that was pretty funny. Because he knew how difficult that was.
